humanoid.description: An upright biped. Axes run -1 to 1 with 0 neutral, unless noted. Every combination of these values is guaranteed to produce a valid body; a reader that clamps out-of-range values to the stated bounds will always be able to build one.

height.description: Standing height in millimetres. Extreme builds may exceed this slightly, since a body that cannot be constructed is worse than one a little off its nominal stature. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

shoulderWidth.description: Width of the shoulder girdle. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

hipWidth.description: Width of the pelvis. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

limbLength.description: Limb length relative to the torso. Longer limbs raise the pelvis and so shorten the torso at a fixed stature. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

neckLength.description: Neck length. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

headSize.description: Head size. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

headBreadth.description: How broad the skull is across, at a fixed head size: negative is a narrow head, positive a broad one. It scales the head's lateral half-extent only, so a broad skull is broad from the parietal down through the angle of the jaw while staying exactly as deep and as tall. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

faceLength.description: How long the face is below the eyes, at a fixed head size: negative is a short face, positive a long one. It moves the head's joint up its own neck, so what changes is how much of the skull sits below it - the jaw, the chin and the whole feature stack - while the cranium above is untouched. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

extremitySize.description: Hand and foot size. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

chestVolume.description: How much chest there is, over what femininity, mass, bodyFat and age already predict (#273). An offset on the derived chest and not a slider of its own: zero is whatever the composites came to, so a record keeps meaning what it meant when the formulas improve. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

chestProjection.description: How far the chest stands off the ribcage against how far it spreads across it, at a fixed volume: negative spreads it, positive stands it off. The shape axis rather than the size one, the same separation headSize and faceLength exist to make. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

chestLift.description: How high the chest sits, over what age and bodyFat predict: positive lifts it and refuses the descent ageing asks for, negative lets it hang. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

chestSpacing.description: How far apart the pair sits, over the azimuth the shape derives: negative is close-set, positive wide. An angle about the trunk's own axis rather than a lateral offset, so the separation a body delivers does not depend on how far its chest stands off. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

chestFullness.description: Where the volume sits between the upper pole and the lower one, over the split the shape derives: positive is a fuller lower pole, negative an evenly divided one, at a fixed volume and projection. Not a second ptosis axis - ageing descends the peak toward a fold that holds still, while this moves the split and the fold under it together. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

quadruped.description: A four-legged creature. Axes run -1 to 1 with 0 neutral, unless noted. Its girth is the composites': mass, bodyFat and age reach it at sites of its own, and femininity does not (#178).

height.description: Height of the back line in millimetres. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

bodyLength.description: Body length from shoulder to hip. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

legLength.description: Legginess. Longer legs slim the body at a fixed back height. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

neckLength.description: Neck length. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

headSize.description: Head size. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

tailLength.description: Tail length. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

family.description: Which kind of animal this is rolled as (#366): the centre a re-roll draws every axis around. The body is its axes and never this name, so a reader that does not recognise a value should read it as a dog and keep the body the axes describe; only the centre of its next roll is lost.

hybrid.description: The second family of a cross, when this is one, and absent when it is not. A cross is rolled between its two families, `blend` of the way toward this one; a cross of a family with itself is no cross. A value a reader does not recognise reads as a dog, as for `family`.

blend.description: How far a cross is rolled toward its `hybrid` family, in thousandths: 0 none of the way, 1000 all of it. Always 0 on a body that is not a cross.

muzzleLength.description: How long the muzzle is: a snub cat's face at the bottom, a horse's long head at the top. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

stance.description: What the legs stand on: flatter feet below 0, the toes of a dog or a cat at 0, the tips of them - a horse's hooves - at 1000, which also raises the hock and the carpus up longer bones of the foot. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

neckCarriage.description: How the neck is carried: low and forward at the bottom, high and arched at the top, the head nodding nose-down as it rises. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

tailCarriage.description: How the tail is carried: hanging at -1000, a sabre curve at 0, raised and curled over the back at 1000; past either end it is carried no further. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

chestDepth.description: How deep the chest is: the withers stand higher over the back and the brisket drops lower toward the elbow as it grows. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

appeal.description: How the whole body is drawn, from naturalistic at the bottom to cute at the top: over the anatomy it grows the head, shortens the muzzle, the neck and the body, and thickens the legs. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

muzzleBreadth.description: How broad the muzzle is, from a narrow wedge at the bottom to a broad box at the top: wider at the nose than at the stop, and squarer in section as it widens. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

stop.description: How the muzzle is set into the skull: a Roman nose, the bridge raised to the forehead's line and bowed, at the bottom; a straight profile in the middle; a deep stop under a high brow at the top. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

eyeSet.description: How the eyes are set: to the front of a flat face at the bottom, looking where the animal goes; on the sides of the skull at the top, watching around it. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

pupil.description: The pupils' shape: round, a vertical slit, or a horizontal bar held level. A part rather than a centre, so it is kept whatever a reader makes of `family`; a value a reader does not recognise reads as round.

earSize.description: How large the ears are against the head. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

earPoint.description: How the ears end: round-tipped leaves at the bottom, pointed triangles at the top. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

earCarriage.description: How the ears are carried: dropped and hanging beside the face at the bottom, folded back in a rose in the middle, pricked up at the top. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

nose.description: What the nose is: a bare leather pad at the muzzle's tip with its nostrils cut into its front, or the soft muzzle a horse breathes through open nostrils. A part rather than a centre, kept whatever a reader makes of `family`; a value a reader does not recognise reads as leather.

feet.description: What the legs stand on: paws with their claws showing, paws with them sheathed, or hooves. A part rather than a centre, kept whatever a reader makes of `family`, and not read off `stance`, which is how the leg stands; a value a reader does not recognise reads as clawed paws.

whiskers.description: How long the whiskers are: none at the bottom, a long fan at the top. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

horn.description: The horn a record could say before ornaments (#402): none, or exactly one spiralled ivory unicorn's horn, which reads as the matching piece in ornaments and goes on being written here by a body wearing exactly that. A creator gives it, or a rare roll does, and a re-roll of the head puts what its seed draws in its place; left off the record when there is none; a value a reader does not recognise reads as none. An ornaments.horn wins over this.

ornaments.description: What it wears on its head, beyond what horn says (#402). A creator gives it, or a rare roll gives one piece (#403); the head's lock holds it, and a re-roll of an unlocked head puts what its seed draws in its place, which is usually nothing. Left off while there is nothing to say.

coat.description: What colour the fur is and how it is marked (#368).

fur.description: How long its fur grows, and where (#369).

quadrupedCoat.description: A quadruped's coat (#368), recorded as coat-genetics loci: a reader derives the colours from the loci, so a coat stays a few small values, a cross can take each locus from either parent, and a creator changes a coat the way it varies in life - a liver dog is the black dog's coat with one locus turned. The genetics are a game's: every locus is open to every family, whichever one carries it in life. A locus value a reader does not recognise reads as that locus's default. Beside the loci, 'colours' holds whatever a creator picked over them (#401).

pigment.description: The pigment the coat is built on: black or liver (brown) eumelanin, or red phaeomelanin alone - a ginger cat, a chestnut horse, a red setter. The bare parts follow it: a liver coat has a liver nose.

dilute.description: Whether the pigment is diluted: black to blue-grey, liver to lilac, red to cream.

agouti.description: How the dark and the light are spread: one colour all over; a light coat tipped dark along the back (sable); every hair banded dark and light, the wild grizzle a tabby's marks are drawn on; a dark coat with light points on the muzzle, brows, chest, legs and under the tail (tanPoints, a black-and-tan); a light coat with dark legs, tail, ear tips and muzzle (bay).

pattern.description: Marks drawn over the coat in its dark pigment: a tabby's narrow stripes (mackerel), its swirls (blotched) or its ticking; round spots; rosettes, rings round a lighter centre; a brindle's thin broken stripes; a dapple's lighter rings netted over a grey.

points.description: Whether the face, ears, legs and tail are darker than a paled body: a colourpoint.

white.description: How much white the coat carries, over every other locus: white feet (socks); feet, chest, a blaze and a tail tip (irish); large patches and most of the underside (piebald); or white nearly all over, colour left on the head and the base of the tail (extreme).

merle.description: Whether the dark is broken into patches over a diluted ground: merle.

roan.description: Whether white hairs are scattered through the body: roan.

dun.description: Whether the body is diluted, with a dark stripe down the back and barred legs: dun.

tortie.description: Whether red and the dark are mixed in patches: a tortoiseshell. A red coat has no dark to mix in, and shows none.

intensity.description: How rich the red runs: cream at -1000, a setter's red at 1000, and past them ivory at -3000 and mahogany at 3000. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

fantasy.description: An unnatural palette the coat's dark and light are drawn in, or none for a natural coat. Rolled as a rarity.

marks.description: The seed the coat's spots, stripes and patches are laid out from, so its marks survive the wire and can be thrown again on their own.

colours.description: The colours a creator picked over what the loci derive (#401), or a rare roll did (#403); the colouring's lock holds them, and a re-roll of an unlocked colouring puts what its seed draws in their place, which is usually nothing. Left off while none is.

quadrupedOrnaments.description: What a beast wears on its head (#402): each piece optional and absent until given. A piece's sizes are shares of the head's radius, so it scales with the head and fits every family and cross. A key a reader does not recognise is ignored.

horn.description: One horn on the middle of the forehead, riding the head: a unicorn's. A horn exactly the defaults below is written as the plan's own horn key instead.

pairedHorns.description: A horn either side of the crown in front of the ears, riding the head: a bull's, a ram's.

upperFangs.description: A fang either side of the upper lip, hanging outside the shut jaw and riding the head: a sabre-tooth's.

lowerFangs.description: A small fang either side of the lower jaw, riding the jaw and opening with the mouth, outside the upper lip where it reaches it.

tusks.description: A tusk either side of the lower jaw, riding the jaw and opening with the mouth, rising outside the upper lip: a boar's.

antlers.description: A branching antler either side of the crown in front of the ears, riding the head: a stag's.

quadrupedOrnament.description: One head ornament's shape and colours (#402). Readers clamp to these bounds, and an absent number reads as its default here: a unicorn's horn.

length.description: Base to tip along its line, as a share of the head's radius, thousandths.

thickness.description: Its radius at the base, as a share of the head's radius, thousandths.

taper.description: How much of its radius it has lost at the tip, thousandths.

curve.description: How far its line turns from base to tip, in thousandths of a whole turn, tightening toward the tip and stepping aside to clear itself past half a turn. A horn or an antler's positive curve turns up or forward, its negative back and down, a ram's curl; a fang's or a tusk's positive turns its tip back toward the throat.

twist.description: How far its flutes turn about it from base to tip, in thousandths of a whole turn. Nothing shows without flutes.

flutes.description: How deep its flutes are, as a share of its radius, thousandths: none at zero.

base.description: Its colour at the base. Ivory if absent. Three channels of sRGB, thousandths.

tip.description: Its colour at the tip. Ivory if absent. Three channels of sRGB, thousandths.

quadrupedAntlers.description: A pair of antlers (#402): a beam shaped as any other ornament is, and what its branching needs. Readers clamp to these bounds, and an absent number reads as its default here. The numbers a beam shares with any ornament default as one does, a unicorn's horn, so a writer gives them all; a stag's are length 2300, thickness 110, taper 650, curve 140, no flutes.

length.description: Base to tip along its line, as a share of the head's radius, thousandths.

thickness.description: Its radius at the base, as a share of the head's radius, thousandths.

taper.description: How much of its radius it has lost at the tip, thousandths.

curve.description: How far its line turns from base to tip, in thousandths of a whole turn, tightening toward the tip and stepping aside to clear itself past half a turn. A horn or an antler's positive curve turns up or forward, its negative back and down, a ram's curl; a fang's or a tusk's positive turns its tip back toward the throat.

twist.description: How far its flutes turn about it from base to tip, in thousandths of a whole turn. Nothing shows without flutes.

flutes.description: How deep its flutes are, as a share of its radius, thousandths: none at zero.

base.description: The beam's colour at the skull. Ivory if absent. Three channels of sRGB, thousandths.

tip.description: The colour its points run to. Ivory if absent. Three channels of sRGB, thousandths.

points.description: How many points each antler ends in, the beam's own tip among them: a count, not thousandths.

fork.description: How wide its tines fork from the beam, from almost along it to almost square to it, thousandths.

quadrupedCoatColours.description: The colours a creator picked for a coat (#401), free rather than points on a pigment ramp, as an iris's are. Each is absent until picked, and absent means what the loci derive. A picked colour wins outright over the loci: dilute, intensity and fantasy do not touch it, and marks keep their layout. A colour a reader does not recognise the name of is ignored.

dark.description: The dark pigment: marks, tips, points, and a dark coat's whole ground. Three channels of sRGB, thousandths.

light.description: The light pigment: tan, a bay's body, a tabby's ground, a red coat's whole ground, a colourpoint's paled body, a dun's diluted body and a dark merle's diluted ground. Three channels of sRGB, thousandths.

white.description: White markings: white spotting and a roan's white hairs. Three channels of sRGB, thousandths.

leather.description: The nose and the pads, under white as well. Three channels of sRGB, thousandths.

horn.description: The claws and the hooves, under white as well. Three channels of sRGB, thousandths.

mane.description: The mane and the forelock, and the skin along the crest under them. Draws nothing on a beast with no mane. Three channels of sRGB, thousandths.

tail.description: The tail, skin and fur, fading in from the rump. Three channels of sRGB, thousandths.

quadrupedFur.description: How long a quadruped's fur grows where a beast grows long hair (#369): each zone a length, none at 0, as a share of the zone's own full length, which scales with the body. Everywhere else the coat is painted. A reader that knows nothing of fur draws the beast bald, which is what an absent field means.

mane.description: A mane down the neck's crest, and a forelock between the ears. Thousandths, 0 to 3000: 1000 is long, and past it the exploration envelope (#160) runs on; readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

ruff.description: A ruff round the neck and over the chest's front. Thousandths, 0 to 3000: 1000 is long, and past it the exploration envelope (#160) runs on; readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

tail.description: A brush along the tail: short fur fluffs, long hair hangs. Thousandths, 0 to 3000: 1000 is long, and past it the exploration envelope (#160) runs on; readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

feathering.description: Feathering down the back of the fetlocks. Thousandths, 0 to 3000: 1000 is long, and past it the exploration envelope (#160) runs on; readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

tufts.description: Tufts at the ears' tips. Thousandths, 0 to 3000: 1000 is long, and past it the exploration envelope (#160) runs on; readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

maneStiffness.description: How stiff the mane is (#389): at 0 it lies flat over the neck and drapes, at 1000 it stands straight up off the crest, a zebra's or a hogged mane; between, it stands further the stiffer it is before it bends over and falls. Its length stays mane's. Never rolled: a beast starts at the default and its owner changes it. Thousandths, 0 to 1000; readers clamp to these bounds. Left off at the default.

composites.description: The high-level description of a body: axes named for something about a person rather than about a body part, each fanning out through formulas to many quantities at once. The per-region axes on an archetype apply as offsets on top of what these derive. Kept beside the archetype rather than inside it because the body, the skull and the skin all read them. Shape axes are thousandths as elsewhere; bodyFat is thousandths of a fraction and age is whole years, not thousandths.

femininity.description: Where the body sits between the masculine and feminine references: -1000 fully masculine, +1000 fully feminine, 0 the midpoint of the two. Read by the frame, the fat distribution and the skull together, so a body cannot disagree with itself about it. A person's axis: a quadruped does not read it, and a re-roll of one keeps the value stored (#178).

mass.description: How much body there is, from slight to heavy. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Sets the girth budget; bodyFat decides how it is spent and where. A heavier body carries it in the fleshy sites and barely at all in the bony ones.

bodyFat.description: What share of the body is fat, in thousandths of a fraction: 30 is about the essential fat of a very lean athlete and 600 is past where a silhouette keeps changing. Not stretched past its ends the way a shape axis is, because a negative fraction is not a leaner person but an absence of one.

age.description: How old the body is, in WHOLE YEARS rather than thousandths. Adults only: child proportions are a different envelope and a separate decision, not the bottom of this slider.

skin.description: A body's complexion. Axes are thousandths, as elsewhere: the AT Protocol data model has no floating-point type. Every combination is a usable complexion.

melanin.description: Base depth of tone, from palest to deepest. Thousandths, 0 to 1000.

undertone.description: Hue beneath the tone: -1000 cool and pink, +1000 warm and olive.

blush.description: How much blood shows through at cheeks, ears, and knuckles. Thousandths, 0 to 1000.

eyes.description: How a body's eyes are shaped and set. Axes are thousandths, as elsewhere: the AT Protocol data model has no floating-point type. Eyes are geometry that moves rather than a painted feature, so these place a globe and the lids that close over it.

size.description: Eye size, as a fraction of the head's radius. Thousandths, -1000 to 2000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

spacing.description: How far apart the eyes are set: -1000 close, +1000 wide. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

depth.description: How deeply the eyes are set: -1000 protruding, +1000 sunken. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

aperture.description: How far open the lids rest: 0 shut, 1000 wide. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

inner.description: The iris beside the pupil, in sRGB. Two colours with a gradient between them, the way hair fades from roots to tips: this one at the pupil's edge, 'outer' at the periphery. Three channels, thousandths. Free rather than a point on a pigment ramp, so fantasy eyes need no special case.

outer.description: The iris at its periphery, in sRGB, faded to from 'inner' across the disc. Three channels, thousandths.

ring.description: The limbal ring around the iris, in sRGB — the circle that makes an iris read as an iris rather than a coloured disc. Three channels, thousandths.

outfit.description: What a body is wearing: a top and a pair of trousers, close-fitting garments cut from the body's own surface a few millimetres outside it, so they fit any wearer without being re-cut and cannot intersect the body. Records written before symbios-avatar 0.10 carried the fields sleeve and leg (cut names) and topHue, topShade, legHue and legShade (thousandths) instead; a reader of such a record should read the cut names bare, forearm and wrist as sleeve lengths 0, 600 and 1000, shorts, calf and ankle as trouser lengths 175, 775 and 1000 (an unknown name as the garment's default length), and the hue and shade as the colour the reference implementation's dye function makes of them. Nothing writes those fields any more.

top.description: The top. Its length is how far its sleeves run.

trousers.description: The trousers. Their length is how far their legs run.

top.description: A top: the chest and the abdomen, and each arm as far as its length.

colour.description: The colour it is dyed, in sRGB thousandths. Free rather than a point on a ramp, as hair colours are. A texture is multiplied by it, so white shows a texture as its generator paints it.

length.description: How far down the limbs it runs, in thousandths of the limb: 0 the limb's root, 500 its middle joint, 1000 its end. Each half is a share of that segment's own bone, so a value names the same landmark on every body, and the hem is a ring square to the limb. For a top: 0 is sleeveless, 500 to the elbow, 1000 to the wrist.

texture.description: What it is made of, if not plain dyed cloth. Absent for plain cloth.

trousers.description: A pair of trousers: the pelvis, and each leg as far as its length.

colour.description: The colour it is dyed, in sRGB thousandths, as the top's is.

length.description: How far down the limbs it runs, in thousandths of the limb: 0 the limb's root, 500 its middle joint, 1000 its end. Each half is a share of that segment's own bone, so a value names the same landmark on every body, and the hem is a ring square to the limb. For trousers: 500 is the knee and 1000 the ankle. The floor, 175, is shorts a third of the way down the thigh; any shorter bares the crotch.

texture.description: What they are made of, if not plain dyed cloth. Absent for plain cloth.

garmentTexture.description: A tileable surface from symbios-texture laid over a garment, multiplied by the garment's colour and baked into the avatar's cloth atlas.

surface.description: The surface generator's configuration in the ecosystem's texture wire form, the same symbios-overlands writes into its material records: the generator's name under $type (one of the registry's tileable surfaces - Fabric, Metal, Chitin, Truchet and the rest; never a card or a sprite), the config's own field names, and every float as an integer in ten-thousandths. A field left out takes the generator's default. A reader that does not know the $type should keep the object as it is and draw the garment in its plain colour.

scale.description: How many times the tile repeats per metre of cloth, in thousandths: 4000 lays a 25 cm tile.

rotation.description: How far the pattern is turned, in thousandths of a degree, counter-clockwise as the garment is seen from outside.

face.description: How prominent a body's facial features are, and how wide. Placed from the published proportion canons - the face divides into thirds from hairline to brow to the base of the nose to the chin, and into fifths across, one fifth being an eye's width - so the prominence axes say how far each feature stands out, not where it sits, and the width axes say how far it reaches across. The skull's own breadth and the face's length are not here: they are properties of the body plan, since they are built into the body rather than carved into it. Thousandths, as elsewhere: the AT Protocol data model has no floating-point type.

nose.description: How far the nose stands out: 0 flat, 1000 prominent. Thousandths. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

noseWidth.description: How wide the nose is across the wings: 0 narrow, 1000 broad. Independent of how far it stands out. Thousandths. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

brow.description: How heavy the brow ridge is. Thousandths, -1000 to 2000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

mouth.description: How full the lips are. Thousandths, -1000 to 2000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

mouthWidth.description: How wide the mouth is, corner to corner. Independent of how full the lips are. Thousandths, -1000 to 2000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

ears.description: How far the ears stand out from the head. Thousandths, -1000 to 2000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

hairCut.description: How one region of hair is cut. Thousandths, as elsewhere: the AT Protocol data model has no floating-point type.

length.description: How far the hair runs past the region it grows from. 0 is cropped to the skin.

thickness.description: How wide each element of hair is. Width costs nothing to draw, so this is the axis a reader should reach for before density.

density.description: How many elements are grown, as a share of what the region can hold. A reader may draw fewer for distant or low-end rendering, which does not change the record.

droop.description: How far the hair gives up its own body and falls with the ground. 0 stands off the skin, 1000 lies flat on it.

hairPaint.description: Hair painted into the skin's own colour, under whatever is grown on top of it. It is what stops thin hair reading as none, and it is the whole of a region a record asks for without geometry: a shaved jaw, a drawn-on brow.

density.description: How much of the skin it covers. Density rather than opacity: at 1000 the skin under the mask is that colour, and between the two the grain shows through, which is what stubble is.

colour.description: What colour, in sRGB. Three channels, thousandths.

scalpRegion.description: Where hair may grow on the scalp: the hairline, and how it recedes.

line.description: Where the hairline sits. -1000 receding, +1000 low on the brow. The whole curve moves together.

temples.description: How deeply the hairline notches back at the temples. 0 is square across the brow and 1000 is two deep bays. Separate from the line because recession is not a raised hairline: a hairline that moved up as a whole is a high forehead, and one that kept its midline peak while the corners went back is what the word recession means.

nape.description: Where the hair stops at the back. -1000 shaved high up the nape, +1000 low onto the neck.

browRegion.description: Where the eyebrows sit. These say where the brow IS, which both layers obey, rather than what is grown on it: changing a haircut does not move a brow ridge.

rise.description: How high the brow sits over the eye. -1000 low and heavy, +1000 high.

apart.description: How far apart the two are. -1000 nearly meeting, +1000 well parted.

reach.description: How far the tail runs past the eye's outer corner. -1000 short, +1000 long.

arch.description: How much the brow arches. -1000 a straight bar, +1000 a high curve. Zero is the arch an ordinary brow has, not a flat one.

moustacheRegion.description: Where hair may grow on the upper lip.

width.description: How far past the mouth's corners it grows. -1000 narrow, +1000 wide.

drop.description: How far down toward the vermilion it grows. -1000 shy of it, +1000 onto its border.

chinRegion.description: Where hair may grow on the chin and the plane under it.

width.description: How wide the patch is. -1000 a narrow tuft, +1000 the whole chin.

under.description: How far under the jaw it reaches. -1000 the chin's front only, +1000 well back along the submental plane.

rise.description: How far up toward the lower lip it grows. -1000 low on the chin, +1000 to the lip's own border.

flankRegion.description: Where hair may grow on the flanks of the jaw, from the sideburn down over the jawline.

cheek.description: How high up the cheek it grows. -1000 a low beard line, +1000 high on the cheekbone.

under.description: How far below the jawline it rides. -1000 stopping on the border, +1000 well down the neck.

sideburn.description: How far forward of the ear the sideburn begins. -1000 well back, +1000 onto the cheek.

follicleRegions.description: Where each of the five kinds of hair may grow on one head. Shape rather than style: these move where hair MAY be, which both layers obey, and say nothing about what is grown there. A hairline is a property of a head and stays where it is when somebody changes their haircut.

scalpStyle.description: The hair of the head. One name, plus whatever axis that style carries; a style with no axis of its own carries none.

name.description: Which style. Readers that do not recognise a value should draw nothing rather than substitute another style: a haircut nobody chose is worse than none. They should still load the rest of the record, and keep the unrecognised style object as it was when they write the record back unless the owner has chosen another style.

fringe.description: BOB: what the front does. 0 swept to the temples, parted, hanging beside the face; a little more a fringe ending just above the brow; 1000 a fringe well above it. A fringe's length is a share of the forehead, never of the cut, so no value hangs over the face. CAP: how deep the sculpted notch over the brow is cut back, 0 at the hairline and 1000 about 22 mm behind it.

volume.description: SLICK_BACK only: how much the front rises over the forehead. 0 combed flat, 1000 a full pompadour.

length.description: BELL only: how far the hem falls. 0 just past the hairline, 1000 to the jawline - measured in the head's own radii, since heads disagree by half about how many millimetres that is.

weight.description: LONG only: how much longer the back is than the sides. 0 even all round, 1000 strongly back-weighted.

tail.description: TIED_BACK only: where the tail is gathered. 0 at the nape, 1000 high on the crown.

curl.description: CURLY only: how tight the coil is. 0 a loose wave, 1000 a tight curl.

height.description: BUN: where the ball of gathered hair sits, as a share of the back of the head. 0 a bun at the nape, 1000 a top knot on the crown. CREST: how tall the fin along the midline is, 0 a low ridge and 1000 a full crest - the sides are shaved either way.

size.description: AFRO only: how far the mass stands off the head. 0 close-cropped coils at the hairline, 1000 a full crown that comes down over the ears - measured in the head's own radii.

rows.description: BRAIDS only: how many cornrows run down the head. 0 four broad ones, 1000 ten.

browStyle.description: The eyebrows. Most faces should have one drawn even where none is grown: a bare brow ridge reads as a mannequin from across a room.

sweep.description: HANDLEBAR only: how far the ends sweep past the mouth's corners. 0 barely past them, 1000 a full waxed curl.

ride.description: PENCIL only: how high the line sits. 0 on the lip's own border, 1000 halfway to the nostrils.

flare.description: SCULPTED only: how far the solid's ends flare past the mouth's corners. 0 a chevron, 1000 a handlebar turned up.

point.description: GOATEE only: how the hang ends. 0 a rounded tuft, 1000 drawn to a point.

twist.description: BRAIDED only: how tightly the rope turns. 0 a loose rope, 1000 a hard twist.

length.description: SCULPTED only: how far the solid mass hangs below the chin. 0 a short boxed beard, 1000 a long spade.

drop.description: SIDEBURNS only: how far down the strip runs. 0 a tab beside the ear, 1000 down to the jaw's corner.

reach.description: FULL_CONNECT only: how far below the jawline the beard rides. 0 stopping on the crease, 1000 down onto the upper neck.

scalpTress.description: The hair of the head, both layers.

style.description: Which base style is grown here, and its own axis if it has one. A style of 'none' grows no geometry, which is how a record asks for a region that is painted and not grown.

roots.description: The colour at the roots, in sRGB. Free rather than a point on a pigment ramp, so that grey and dyed hair need no special case.

tips.description: The colour at the tips, likewise, faded to along each element as a vertex colour.

skin.description: The hair painted into the skin under this region.

hair.description: The hair on a body's head: five follicle regions, each drawn in two layers over one shared mask — hair painted into the skin, and low-poly geometry grown on top of it. Absent means the default, which is a cropped head with full brows and no facial hair. Both layers read the same mask, so a reader that draws only the painted layer still puts hair where the record says it is.

regions.description: Where each kind of hair may grow, which both layers obey.
